text: The Earth is approximately spherical in shape, slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator. This has been confirmed by satellite imagery, space travel, and centuries of scientific observation.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure. This temperature changes with altitude and pressure.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second. This is a fundamental constant of nature and is denoted by the symbol 'c'.

Climate change is primarily caused by human activities, particularly the emission of greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane. The scientific consensus is overwhelming, with 97% of climate scientists agreeing on this.
Vaccines are safe and effective at preventing diseases. They have been responsible for the eradication or near-eradication of many deadly diseases including smallpox and polio.
The Moon orbits Earth at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometers (238,855 miles). The Moon's gravitational pull causes ocean tides on Earth.
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) carries genetic information in living organisms. It has a double helix structure discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953.
The theory of evolution by natural selection, proposed by Charles Darwin, explains how species change over time through inherited traits that improve survival and reproduction.
Smoking tobacco significantly increases the risk of lung cancer, heart disease, stroke, and many other serious health conditions. This is supported by decades of research.
Antibiotics are effective against bacterial infections but do not work against viral infections like the common cold or flu. Overuse of antibiotics can lead to antibiotic resistance.
The Sun is approximately 93 million miles (150 million kilometers) from Earth. This distance is called an Astronomical Unit (AU) and varies slightly due to Earth's elliptical orbit.
Humans have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs. Genetic disorders can occur when there are abnormalities in chromosome number or structure.
The Great Wall of China is approximately 13,170 miles (21,196 kilometers) long. It was built over many centuries to protect Chinese states from invasions.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy, producing oxygen as a byproduct. This process is essential for life on Earth.
Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth at 29,032 feet (8,849 meters) above sea level. It is located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and Tibet.
The human brain contains approximately 86 billion neurons. It uses about 20% of the body's energy despite being only 2% of body weight.
Coffee is one of the most traded commodities in the world. It contains caffeine, a natural stimulant that affects the central nervous system.
Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It is now one of the most popular programming languages, especially for data science and machine learning.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth, covering more than 63 million square miles. It contains approximately 25,000 islands.
Regular exercise reduces the risk of chronic diseases including heart disease, diabetes, and certain cancers. The WHO recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week.
